gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients present with histologically confirmed diagnosis of an H3.1K27M or H3.3K27M-mutated diffuse midline glioma WHO grade IV

candidate_evidence.quote: One vial of Tecentriq® (1200 mg) will be administered as an intravenous (i.v.) infusion over 60 minutes every 3 weeks starting 4 weeks after radiotherapy.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: The primary immunogenicity endpoint is the presence of an H3K27M-specific T-cell response.

role_evidence.quote: Based on these observations we hypothesize that checkpoint inhibition targeting PD-L1 is required for optimal amplification of a vaccine-induced H3K27M-specific T cell response.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: checkpoint inhibition targeting PD-L1 to amplify vaccine-induced H3K27M-specific T cell response

role_evidence.quote: [BIOLOGICAL] H3K27M peptide vaccine: The H3K27M peptide vaccine is injected subcutaneously (s.c.).

agents.drug_class_hint: long peptide cancer vaccine against H3K27M neoepitope

role_evidence.quote: The H3K27M peptide vaccine is administered in combination with topical Imiquimod that serves as an adjuvant.

agents.drug_class_hint: topical TLR7 agonist used as vaccine adjuvant

source_quote.quote: Tumoral H3.1K27M or H3.3K27M mutation proven by immunohistochemistry or H3 DNA sequencing

coder_notes: Population is H3K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma only; glioblastoma appears only in keywords, so not_glioblastoma. Atezolizumab is the only non-excluded investigational drug (pembrolizumab + vaccine worked example), hence experimental_monotherapy; regimen is combination because of vaccine and radiotherapy. H3K27M eligibility is matched mechanistically to the vaccine (an excluded intervention type), not to atezolizumab, so candidate_matched is false. Imiquimod coded supportive (vaccine adjuvant, no antitumour hypothesis stated); adjudicator may prefer otherwise.
